## What the additions prove

| Group | Named theorems | Scope |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Reflection and determinants | 8 | Explicit two-band formula, sublattice algebra, finite restriction under conjugacy, involution determinant and determinant-norm log-odds |
| Odd part and finite increments | 5 | Correct sign; even-part cancellation; exact relation between rate differences and offset differences |
| Band-product bound | 4 | Polynomial identity, strict bound with positive band-edge hypotheses, critical counterexample, normalized magnitude below one |
| Tanh and asymmetry | 3 | Exact exponential and finite positive-endpoint identities |
| Shear | 2 | Determinant one together with failure of the proposed parity eigenvector relation |
| Logistic counterexample | 4 | Positive complementary scalar probabilities, reflection and arbitrary/linearly growing offset |
| Monotonicity counterexample | 4 | Strictly positive sequence bounded by one half, tending to one half, with a finite drop; negation of the claimed implication |

## Consequences for the supplied endpoint pass

The sublattice/determinant reformulation is useful. It does not by itself prove boundedness of the odd log-determinant contribution: the exact logistic family has complement reflection and growing offset. The proposed inference from bounded convergence to monotonicity is false even with the counterexample's values and limit strictly inside (0,1).

The unrestricted band-product strictness claim needs its gap assumptions at v=0. The intended gapped bound is proved with those assumptions explicit.

The magnitude target and signed/parity target remain distinct. The reported odd-block sign alternation must not be combined with an unqualified signed all-odd-length limit.

## Outside certification

No infinite-chain Fourier integration, complete spectral functional-calculus identification, physical Gaussian-state interpretation, or strict covariance positivity theorem is formalized here. The finite block lemma assumes the full conjugacy and proves restriction preserves it. The determinant log-odds is the existing norm-log definition.

No general convergence, geometric rate, compact-uniform estimate, failure of uniformity near criticality, Abel-map phase, full interior spacing, cosmological-constant value or light-needle application is certified. Exact cancellation of the even part does not prove that all growing terms are even.

See ENDPOINT_SCOPE.md. PR #2 and PR #4 are unchanged; PR #5 remains a draft, and nothing is merged.

## Main manuscript correction

The supplied *Constructible Proofs for the Arithmetic Kakeya Conjecture*, arithmetic_kakeya_full_v2.pdf, has a false local-seeding necessity claim in Lemma 4 (p. 4). Its own Figure 3 data give three initial generators at distinct sites, yet force all four vertices, beginning at the vertex with no initial generator. Explicit integer witnesses for all four steps are Lean-checked in KakeyaSeedingControl.

The subset-rank argument of Theorem 2 is **not** refuted: it includes crossing-edge labels as well as internal vertex-generator labels. KakeyaCut checks its column-sum, cancellation, linearity, and rank-one exclusion components.

Appendix A.6 requires two independent generators at one site. Its negative search results therefore cover a restricted family, not the entire claimed candidate class. For six sites/seven labels, it omits 6860 three-distinct-site generator subsets out of 11480 total. This does not assert an improved bound, invalidate unrelated broader searches, or claim the omitted family was searched here. See KAKEYA_SEEDING_CORRECTION.md for the exact witness table and replacement scope.

## Added modules

| Module | Named theorems | Scope |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| RestrictionBridge | 5 | Finite boundary-flux identity; restricted edge-cover capacity transfer |
| KakeyaExtension | 5 | Exact power density; conditional score exclusion; positive-density eventual growth |
| EarthMoon | 13 | Explicit C7[K4] finite graph counts, triangle-free join graph, proper 10-coloring; contradiction assuming layer Euler bounds |
| FCSMoments | 8 | Four-point moment counterexample and determination by moments 0–3 |
| KakeyaSeedingControl | 11 | Figure 3 first witness, full forcing sequence, no local seed, label admissibility and pattern counts |
| KakeyaCut | 9 | Actual two-coordinate generator restriction/cancellation and rank-one obstruction |
| KakeyaForcingLinear | 10 | Kernel criterion, dual obstruction, coordinate invariance, conditional real projector criterion, inverse-on-kernel identities, label normalization |
| KakeyaAtlasFamily | 18 | Exact rational family, arbitrary-order reachability, completion iff q=2, explicit completing witnesses and q=1 stall |
| KakeyaAtlasProjector | 16 | Exact kernel line, symmetric idempotent projector, kernel image/fixing, target response 1/13 |

PR #3 already verifies the original supplied AK/FCS files and prior scoped corrections; those are not new results here.

## Atlas result and interpretation

For the fixed four-vertex Figure 3 graph and seed arrangement, changing the edge label to (1,q) yields completion **if and only if q=2** over rational coefficients and every fresh-vertex forcing order. q=1 can force g4 initially but then stalls; every other q cannot start. q=-1 is separately excluded as an inadmissible Kakeya edge label. This is a classification of one fixed family, not a search over all constructible graphs.

For q=2, the initial g3 constraint kernel is exactly the line spanned by c=(-1,-1,1,-1,2,-1,-2). The rational projector P=c cᵀ/13 is symmetric, idempotent, maps into the kernel and fixes it. The target response is exactly 1/13>0. The real inner-product theorem separately states the kernel-image, kernel-fixing and symmetry hypotheses required for its forcing criterion.

This supplies exact algebra for the atlas/projector interpretation. The shifted-operator and inverse-on-kernel identities do not certify an analytic contour integral or identify P as a Riesz integral. See ATLAS_LEAN_SCOPE.md.

## Outside certification / next work

- Assemble the full quantified iterative subset-rank theorem and its lattice-rank conclusion.
- Repair and rerun the incomplete seeded enumeration; no new Kakeya record established. The classified family still scores 7/4 > 67/40, so changing only its parameter cannot reach the target.
- Formalize rational-to-integer clearing in a general family, a general constructibility grammar, and any analytic contour-integral identification.
- Formalize the topological planarity-to-Euler bridge and graph chromatic lower bound; no Epoch Earth–Moon solution.
- Establish physical/independent-mode realizability for FCS uses.
- No new certification of the Offset manuscript's full Rice–Mele asymptotic, Abel-map phase, full interior spacing, cosmological-constant value, or light-needle application.
- The common restriction/cancellation structure is mathematically explicit; identifying it with gravity requires a separate model and proof.

See EXTENSION_SCOPE.md and ATLAS_LEAN_SCOPE.md.
